memo.verdict: Neutral on the shares, bullish on the business. Park Addtech (ADDT.B-SE) at SEK 343.8 (2026-10-02) on price, not on quality; conviction medium. The case is not invalidated and does not progress. Two triggers to progress: (1) the shares at or below about SEK 313 with the case intact, where the modal path gives 20% a year over eighteen months; or (2) organic growth printing at 3% or more for two consecutive quarters with the multiple no higher than today's 28.6x 24-month-forward earnings, which moves the modal multiple to the cleared branch (29x) and the eighteen-month return to about 18% a year, a B on the framework's anchors. The park rule (a D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability) is not triggered: management B (RA 3, E 1, BB 4), business quality B (E 2, BB 2), predictability C (RA 8, E 2, BB 4), trackability C (RA 7, E 2, BB 4). Invalidation at this price: organic growth at or below 0% in Q2 and Q3 FY2027 with a book-to-bill below 100%, or the weighted manufacturing PMI back below 50.
case: - The thesis in the record's words: Addtech is a proven Swedish decentralised compounder whose adjusted earnings should grow about 12% a year as it scales its acquisition engine and lifts its margin structurally through proprietary mix and real pricing, while its organic volume, flat for eleven quarters, is only now turning in the order book. At SEK 343.8 the shares trade at 28.6x 24-month-forward earnings, the highest multiple in the 59-stock comparison set, so they already pay for that compounding: the 'Modal return' is 12.8% a year over eighteen months and 12.0% a year over three years against the 20% bar. Great business, priced for it; watch the organic line and the price.

- The change inside the company is structural and is the spine of the case. On 1 October 2025 five business areas became six (Safety carved out of Energy and Electrification, about 20 companies, around SEK 3.0 to 3.5 billion of revenue at an estimated 13.5% EBITA margin) and twelve business units became fifteen; Energy was narrowed to transmission and distribution; two internal managers (Marcus Johansson, Åsa Skarbrandt) joined Group Management; the chief financial officer said in September 2026 that the structure supports 15 to 20 acquisitions a year, up from 10 to 15; sales outside the Nordics reached 42% in FY2026; Q1 FY2027 added Staka Holding and Nijhuis Engineering (Netherlands), RTL Materials (United Kingdom, August 2026, GBP 11 million of sales) and RAMME Electric Machines (Germany) earlier; pricing is applied within days of supplier moves across customised and proprietary products that are two-thirds of sales (proprietary and own brands 35%, customised 30%, trading 35%). The screen's red flags are absent: no caretaker chief executive, an executed and restated structure change, bolt-ons of SEK 50m to SEK 500m of turnover, leverage 1.3x, no debt-funded buyback. 'Change Forces' (E 1, BB 1) B; 'Internal forces' B; 'External forces' B.

- The external demand force has turned from headwind to early tailwind and is the swing factor. The 33/66 weighted Swedish and Eurozone manufacturing PMI crossed 53 in June 2026, after which the group's organic growth has historically accelerated two to five quarters later, outgrowing industrial production by about 1.5 percentage points a year; the Q1 FY2027 book-to-bill was slightly above 100%; Automation's orders improved sequentially for five consecutive quarters; grid orders recovered after the transmission operators' delays; Svenska Kraftnät plans a 50% investment increase in 2026; defence (about 4% of group sales, about 15% of Automation) rides EU programmes of up to EUR 800 billion by 2030; the cohort's organic lines have already turned (Indutrade +5%, Lagercrantz +6%, Sdiptech +11%), which says Addtech lags on Energy comparisons and sawmills rather than losing share. Against: eleven flat quarters; sawmills about 5% of EBITA with some subsidiaries' revenues down 30% to 50% from pandemic peaks and a 40% earnings drop modelled in the niche; Process postponements; hedged timing language ("takes a couple of quarters"). Direction by force: demand tailwind forming; competition neutral (acquisition multiples stable at a 6.8x median for Addtech, 6.6x Lagercrantz, 6.7x Lifco, 8.6x Indutrade; the Nordic target market tightening, private equity easing); disruption a slow headwind (platform procurement, against the commoditised third); political and regulatory tailwind (EU Battery Regulation recycled-content mandates of 16% cobalt and 6% lithium by 2031; Germany's Planning and Procurement Acceleration Act; CSRD, ESRS and CBAM costs the other way); supply neutral (largest supplier about 1% of purchasing; AI data-centre demand lengthening automation component lead times to six to eight months); own cycle turning up; macro headwind (75% of sales outside SEK; a 5% krona appreciation cuts sales by SEK 810m and operating profit by SEK 98m; a 1 point rate move is SEK 57m post-tax; the Riksbank expected at 1.75% through 2026).
counter_case: - At its strongest, the risks report's "false friend": Addtech is a serial acquirer whose headline EBITA grows 11% to 12% on bought earnings and on a margin flattered by project mix and earn-out revaluations (SEK 13m in Q3 FY2026; a 17.3% reported Q4 FY2026 margin that was 16.4% underlying), while the underlying business has not grown its volume for eleven quarters and will not, because its decentralised portfolio is over-exposed to short-cycle Nordic industrial capital spending (60% of the top subsidiaries), because its organic recovery depends on a PMI it does not control, and because in the one area where it should have grown, Energy, with Svenska Kraftnät's budget behind it, sales fell 7% in the latest quarter. On this reading the April 2026 downgrade to Hold was right and the June upgrade premature; the margin step reverses when the mix normalises (the test: sequential gross margin down more than 50 basis points without volume); the acquisition engine faces rising competition in a saturated Nordic market and unfamiliar regulation abroad; and the multiple, at the top of the comparison set, compresses to 20x EV/EBITA and the shares to about SEK 295, a 14% fall, or to the ten-year "conservative" band of 19.4x on earnings, SEK 233 on today's consensus, a 32% fall. The evidence for it is real: eleven flat quarters against a 6% to 6.5% organic norm; two years of EBITA growth below the 15% target (14%, then 12%); the earn-out and underlying-margin adjustments; the Hold-rated view that multiple expansion is capped without organic acceleration; and the risks report's own analysis of competing hypotheses, in which this profile carries the fewest inconsistencies.

- What the record concedes: the eleven quarters; that the organic half of the model is external in its timing; that part of the margin gain is mix that can reverse; that the Energy decline in Q1 FY2027, while explained by comparisons, is not yet reversed in revenue; that coverage is thin enough that the Q1 "beat" (1% on adjusted EBITA; organic 0% against minus 2%) rested on one house's estimate; and that the mark-to-market downside on a de-rating alone is 16% to 23% at a prudent trough and 32% at the ten-year "conservative" band.
triggers: - Progress triggers: the shares at or below about SEK 313 with the case intact (20% a year on the modal path over eighteen months; about SEK 280 on the three-year horizon); or organic growth at 3% or more for two consecutive quarters with the multiple no higher than today's (the cleared branch, 29x, about 18% a year over eighteen months, a B).

- Invalidation at this price: organic growth at or below 0% in Q2 and Q3 FY2027 with a book-to-bill below 100%; the weighted manufacturing PMI back below 50; entry multiples above 8x EBITA; post-acquisition organic growth falling; Automation's margin back toward 11%; a second culture misjudgement of the 2023 kind.

- Alarm levels: organic at or below 0% in Q2 FY2027 with a book-to-bill below 100%; a deal count below ten for a year; net debt to EBITDA above 2.0x; sequential gross-margin compression of more than 50 basis points without volume; net interest rising toward SEK 450m a year or tax above 24%; sell-side EPS cuts of 2 percent or more.

- Dated events: Q2 FY2027 on 2026-10-22; Q3 FY2027 in February 2027; FY2027 year-end in May 2027 (a first full year at a 16%-plus EBITA margin; dividend near SEK 4.00); evidence through FY2027 on whether the deal count reaches 15 to 20.

- Series to watch: the weighted Swedish and Eurozone manufacturing PMI against 53 (lead two to five quarters); Swedish manufacturing inventory indicators; timber prices and sawmill investment signals; Svenska Kraftnät's investment plans and tender activity; EUR/SEK (consensus forecasts toward 10.40 to 10.50 over twelve months); peers' organic prints (Indutrade, Lagercrantz, Lifco, Bufab); Addtech's organic growth and book-to-bill; acquisitions announced and their multiples where disclosed; FactSet consensus EPS revisions.

- Open questions the record could not settle from the files: whether the organic lag against Lagercrantz is local share loss or mix and comparison (unresolved); whether the pricing gains are 2%-plus a year in real terms (not quantified); the raise-to-lower count behind the revision skew (met on net change, not on a count); the overlap with the framework's own track-record and lessons files (not in the folder; the four archetype fits stand in); the live thematics file and the ticker's sidecar (not in the folder; the pin and the research's themes stated instead); the absent pins for GDWN-GB, IDUN.B-SE and TEQ-SE (treated as absent); the earlier Analysis and Judgement memo of 2026-07-06 (not read, by the hold-out rule).
